analysis:
The only change in this batch is a one-line documentation edit in docs/architecture/inference.md (base/head line 1866). It extends the `stop` row of the sampling-parameter table. It describes per-request stop-string scoping: Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans (`ReasoningStopScope`), and the diffusion Gemma block engine matches the whole output with no scope. No executable code, key handling, attestation flow, coordinator contract, encryption path or prefix-cache (T-041) storage logic is modified.

I looked at the surrounding text in both units for threat-model interactions. It covers MTP, sampling, reasoning, constrained JSON, tool-call parsing and MiMo. None of it touches A-001 sealing, TB-002 plaintext handling, TB-011 authorization, or the TB-012/TB-013 add-on surfaces. Scoped stop strings are an output-handling behavior over already-decrypted content inside the provider process. They do not change the trust boundaries or who can see plaintext. Stop-string semantics are consumer-controlled input, but they are matched locally on held-back text and do not alter routing, billing or authorization as documented. The new scoping could in principle change what text is truncated or withheld, but the actual implementation (`EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`, `ReasoningStopScope`) is not in the supplied evidence, so the described behavior cannot be verified from this batch. That is a coverage limit, not a finding. The edit documents behavior and does not invalidate any threat-model assumption. No threat-model update is needed for the doc change itself.
